summary: The starter prompt clearly defines the core goal (Node.js + LangChain agent to categorize transactions and expose a monthly-per-category aggregation). The run environment (Node 24, existing cluster sample_fintech_02, DOCUMENTDB_URI) is supplied in the skill_md, so a builder can start. Several implementation details are left unspecified (driver version, exact document shape and collection name, LLM/provider and env vars, taxonomy contents, seed data, exact agent invocation method, run/test/README conventions, indexes), and the builder will make reasonable defaults or rely on the installed documentdb-* skills for patterns and best practices.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js LangChain agent that reads uncategorised transactions from DocumentDB ... assigns a category from a fixed taxonomy, writes the category back ... and exposes an aggregation endpoint showing monthly spend breakdown by category."
rubric.note: The business problem, user action, and what the sample demonstrates are clear.
Single LangChain agent is explicitly requested.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "Node.js 24 with npm and npx is available."
rubric.note: Node.js runtime version is provided in the run-environment skill_md.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the official mongodb Node.js driver (npm package 'mongodb'), current stable release compatible with MongoDB 7.0 (e.g., mongodb@5.x), and follow documentdb-driver guidance to instantiate a singleton MongoClient reused across the app.
rubric.note: The documentdb-driver skill gives patterns (singleton client) but does not pick an exact driver package/version; the builder must choose a specific npm package/version.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol...) is reachable... use database named sample_fintech_02."
rubric.note: Run environment explicitly gives the cluster tier and database to use.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time. Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture; use a config file or .env.example with a placeholder."
rubric.note: Secrets location for the DocumentDB connection is stated. LLM/model credentials are not specified (see AI components).

rubric.found_in_prompt: "reads uncategorised transactions from DocumentDB" and writes category back to the document; skill_md: "use the database named sample_fintech_02"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Assume a collection named 'transactions' in database 'sample_fintech_02' with documents shaped roughly as: { _id, transactionId, merchant (string), amount (number), date (ISODate), category (string|null|missing), metadata... }. Treat documents with category null/empty/missing as uncategorised.
rubric.note: Prompt and skill_md do not fix collection name or field names; documentdb-data-modeling can guide structure but won't pick exact names.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will add an idempotent seed script (e.g., seed.js) that upserts a small set (dozens) of sample transactions across multiple months containing merchant, amount, and date fields so aggregation can be demonstrated.
rubric.note: No sample-data source, size, license, or loader is specified.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "exposes an aggregation endpoint showing monthly spend breakdown by category" (implies use of MongoDB aggregation pipeline).
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement aggregation with a pipeline that projects year-month from the ISO date (e.g., {$dateToString: {format: "%Y-%m", date: "$date"}}), groups by that and category, and sums amount. Create an index on { date: 1, category: 1 } (or separate single-field indexes) to help aggregation; use documentdb-indexing guidance for index choice.
rubric.note: Index shapes and full list of query patterns are not provided; documentdb-indexing skill can guide decisions but won't strictly mandate parameters.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "uses prompt engineering to instruct the LLM to assign a category from a fixed taxonomy" and "LangChain agent"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use LangChain's Node.js integration with an OpenAI-compatible chat model (e.g., gpt-3.5-turbo or another available model). Model API key provided via environment variable (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY). The app will craft a prompt containing merchant and amount (and optionally date), the in-code taxonomy, few-shot examples, and explicit instruction to return a single category label. The code will validate / map any LLM output to one of the taxonomy values.
rubric.note: Neither provider nor exact model, nor env var names, are specified; these will materially affect integration code.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "exposes an aggregation endpoint showing monthly spend breakdown by category."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide an HTTP server (Express) with at least: GET /monthly-spend that returns JSON per-month/per-category totals. Also provide either POST /run-categorization or a CLI command (npm run categorize) to invoke the LangChain agent to process uncategorized transactions; the builder will choose one and document it.
rubric.note: Prompt does not state how the agent is triggered (HTTP endpoint, scheduler, or manual CLI); that choice will be made by the implementer.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable... Use the database named sample_fintech_02... Do not provision another cluster unless the run policy says Azure writes are allowed; the cluster above is the one to use."
rubric.note: The run environment explicitly directs use of the existing cluster; deployment/provisioning of cloud infra is not required for the sample run.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will include README/run instructions: npm install, copy .env.example to .env, set DOCUMENTDB_URI and model API key, run seed script, start server (npm start), call GET /monthly-spend and run POST /run-categorization or CLI to trigger categorization. Tests (if any) will be described but are not present by default.
rubric.note: No explicit run/test commands are provided.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Acceptance criteria: (1) agent updates documents' category field only for documents that were uncategorized, (2) aggregation endpoint returns JSON grouping by year-month and category with correct sums matching the seeded data, and (3) connection string and model creds are read from env vars and not committed.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't give explicit, testable acceptance criteria.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Default constraints: do not provision new clusters or commit secrets; sample should be small and cost-conscious, not production-grade (no CMK or complex HA changes).
rubric.note: No cost/scale/compliance limits or non-goals were specified.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Follow standard Node.js repo layout: package.json, src/, routes/, scripts/seed.js, .env.example, README.md. Use 'Azure DocumentDB' naming in docs per gallery policy. Pin versions in package.json where reasonable.
rubric.note: Prompt does not provide a required structure or README conventions.

contradictions: Prompt says 'Using the DocumentDB skill' (singular). No single skill named exactly 'DocumentDB' is installed — instead there are many documentdb-* skills (documentdb-driver, documentdb-connection, documentdb-indexing, etc.). The builder will interpret this as 'use the available DocumentDB skills'.
questions_for_author: Which LLM/provider and model should the sample use (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or a different provider)? What environment variable(s) hold the model API key and endpoint?

What is the fixed taxonomy (explicit list of category strings) you want included in-code, or should the builder invent a reasonable finance taxonomy (e.g., Food, Travel, Utilities, Entertainment, Income, Other)?
What is the collection name and exact field names for merchant, amount and date? (If unspecified, should the builder use 'transactions' with fields {merchant, amount, date, category}?)
How should the LangChain agent be invoked in the sample: via an HTTP endpoint, a CLI command, or a background/cron-like process started by the app?
requirements_at_risk: Define the fixed taxonomy (a concrete list of category strings) in the application code — the starter prompt requests a fixed taxonomy but does not provide the actual list; no installed skill will pick the categories.
AI model/provider credentials from environment variables — skill_md sets DOCUMENTDB_URI but does not specify model/provider env vars; prompt omits where model credentials come from.

.env.example that lists every setting with placeholders — skill_md asks never to write connection string and to use .env.example but does not provide the file; the prompt does not require creating it.

Seed script that loads sample data and creates the index idempotently — prompt asks to read uncategorised transactions but does not provide sample-data source or a seed script; no skill will auto-generate sample dataset for this app.

Vector index dimensions and vector index parameter choices — the run environment mentions the cluster is vector-capable, but the prompt does not require embeddings or vector indexes; reference expects vector-dimension alignment if vectors used.
README with prerequisites, setup, run, and cleanup — prompt does not require writing a README or specify its contents.
Unit tests that run without a live cluster — tests are not mentioned; building tests that mock DocumentDB is not covered by prompt or skills.
Dependencies pinned in a requirements.txt (or equivalent pinned package.json entries) — prompt doesn't require pinned dependencies; gallery conventions expect this.

Infrastructure-as-code for the cluster — the run environment already includes a cluster and the prompt forbids provisioning another; the reference asks for infra as code but starter prompt does not provide it.
